narrative.title: The Leftmost Locker Rule
narrative.scenario: A parcel depot files consignments so smaller tracking numbers always sit to the left of larger ones. The receptionist hunting the smallest number in play never needs to open a single locker: she keeps turning left until a locker has no further left wing, and that dead-end locker holds the depot's minimum.
narrative.inputFormat: A binary search tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child).
narrative.outputFormat: Return the minimum value stored in the tree.

testCases.explanation: From 8, turning left twice reaches the leftmost locker 3.
5 has no left child, so it is already the smallest filed value.

hintLevels: Level 1: In a sorted filing rule, the smallest item can never have anything to its left.
Level 2: Walk left while a left wing exists; the walk ends exactly at the minimum.
Level 3: The right subtree is irrelevant — touching it can only meet larger values.
